evidence.note: Root-caused an N=2048 overflow/indexing failure ('Analyze overflow', 'Check int overflow'), applied an int64 fix, then re-verified correctness and benchmarked — targeted diagnosis of a large-N numeric failure.

Traced a Cauchy precision/tolerance miss stage-by-stage ('Pinpoint precision loss', 'Stage-by-stage error', 'Test tf32 for proj', 'fp32 to_out helps'), revised the precision strategy deliberately and re-verified — distinguishing numeric from performance issues.
Isolated a masked/cache-leakage correctness bug ('Test cache leakage', 'Track ptrs across iterations') and fixed it, showing hypothesis-driven debugging rather than blind tweaks.
'Bench reverted' after stream and precision experiments that regressed — recognized falsified changes and backed them out instead of pushing harder.
Debugged a CUDA-graph + regenerated-input ('normal_') mismatch down to tensor identity, root-causing a subtlety in how the grader reuses/regenerates inputs.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly distinguishes correctness failures (2048 overflow, Cauchy precision, mask/cache and graph-input bugs) from performance concerns, root-causes each with targeted diagnostics, applies deliberate design revisions (int64 indexing, fp32/tf32 precision paths), and re-verifies without regressing — even reverting changes that didn't help. This spans multiple distinct failure types across the whole trajectory, matching the level-8 anchor and edging toward 10; it falls short of a clean 10 because the long latency-tuning tail shows some repetitive re-tuning rather than always knowing when to stop on a shape that already cleared the gate.
